Subject: Realtime inference errors impacting triage workflows

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a spike in inference errors at ~08:50 PT that is causing failures in our triage pipelines (errors are 500s from the /v1/generate endpoint). The issue affects ~15% of requests and is blocking critical workflows for on-call nurses.

Attached is a short snippet of the logs from our side and a correlation trace (request ids included). Can you confirm whether this looks like a model regression, a runtime capacity problem, or a routing issue? We don't have a reliable workaround at the moment.

Attachments: nimbus-correlation-ids.txt (text), brief-trace-sample.json (json)

Thanks — we’re available on the phone and can join a bridge.

— Alex

Date: 2026-04-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime inference errors impacting triage workflows — mitigation applied

Alex / team — quick update from the bridge: we identified a mismatched kernel selection on the variant currently routed for Nimbus that causes intermittent 500s under high token-parallelism.

What we did (10:00 PT):
- Rolled back to the previous kernel/profile for the variant (no model weight change)
- Toggled routing to the stable variant for new requests (in-flight requests are being drained)
- No code changes to customer clients required

Can you validate whether request success rates have improved on your side? If you can spare a short test load (5–10 requests across the affected endpoints) that would confirm the fix.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx (draft)

Date: 2026-04-19T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: SEV-3827 — Executive summary, timeline, and action tracker

Alex / Nimbus team — thanks again for your patience and for joining the bridge yesterday. Below is an executive summary and the follow-ups we will own. Happy to schedule a 30-minute review next week to walk the postmortem.

Executive summary (what happened):
- Impact window: 2026-04-18 08:50–10:00 PT (approx) — intermittent 500s on /v1/generate for ~15% of requests
- Root cause: kernel selection mismatch under high token-parallelism causing runtime crashes on the active variant
- Mitigation: rolled back kernel/profile and routed traffic to stable variant at 10:00 PT; success rates returned to baseline within ~12 minutes after in-flight drains

Customer impact and compensation:
- Impacted workflows: triage ingestion pipelines (real-time) — potential patient triage delays (we understand the sensitivity)
- Offer: Redwood will provide a service credit for the impacted window and a technical review session to validate future deploys

Action tracker (owners / ETA):
- Finalize postmortem document and share with customer — Marissa Cole — 2026-04-20 EOD (link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/postmortems/Nimbus-2026-04-18)
- Kernel selection guardrail: add automated validation to release pipeline — Dylan Brooks — 2026-05-02
- Retro with product/release to tighten canary thresholds — Stephanie Nguyen — 2026-04-30
- Provide service credit and legal/finance coordination — Finance (cc track) — 2026-04-23

Attachments: action-tracker-3827.csv (CSV), postmortem-final-link.txt (link stub)

If you prefer a short walkthrough, I can set up a call with the team next week. Please let me know your available times.

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen
